questions.q: Why did the framers make the impeachment wording vague?
a: So future Congresses could remove leaders in changing times
So presidents could interpret the rules for themselves
So state governments could decide each case
So the Supreme Court could settle every dispute
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the wording had to be precise yet adaptable, which is why high crimes and misdemeanors fits.

questions.q: What does the phrase high crimes and misdemeanors allow?
a: Removing a president for malice without a specific crime
Removing a president for unpopular policies alone
Removing a president only after a criminal conviction
Removing a president by a simple majority vote
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes a president need not commit a crime, but must show malicious intentions.

questions.q: Why was Andrew Johnson targeted for impeachment?
a: He was viewed as irritating and racist, not criminal
He was caught ordering a break-in at headquarters
He refused to leave office after losing an election
He sold government secrets to a foreign power
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the House pursued him over character and politics, and the Senate acquitted him.

questions.q: What happened before Richard Nixon could be impeached?
a: He resigned from office
The Senate acquitted him
The House dropped the charges
He pardoned his advisers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Nixon resigned preemptively once his Watergate crimes became clear.

questions.q: What did the seven senators who broke with their party in Johnson's trial do?
a: They put the constitution ahead of party loyalty
They traded their votes for future appointments
They demanded Johnson resign before voting
They delayed the trial until the next election
questions.why: Lesson 3 says they crossed party lines to protect checks and balances, and none were reelected.
